test_title: PYST 32: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which among the following two organisations signed an Memorandum of Understanding to establish an incubation centre promoting innovation in solar energy and green hydrogen in May 2025?

options.text: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited
Defence Research and Development Organisation and National Thermal Power Corporation
National Institution for Transforming India Aayog and Indian Space Research Organisation
National Solar Energy Federation of India and National Institute of Solar Energy

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** is the nodal ministry of the Government of India responsible for all matters relating to new and renewable energy. Its objective is to develop and deploy new and renewable energy for supplementing energy requirements in the country.
 
• The **Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL)** is a **public sector enterprise** in India and one of the largest engineering and manufacturing companies in the country. It has expertise in areas like power generation, transmission, and renewable energy technologies.
 
• In May 2025, the **MNRE** and **BHEL** signed a **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** aimed at establishing an **incubation centre**. The primary goal of this centre is to **promote innovation in solar energy and green hydrogen technologies**.
 
• This collaboration is expected to drive advancements in clean energy solutions, contributing to India's commitment towards **sustainability and reduction of carbon emissions**.
 
• The MoU focuses on fostering **research and development** activities and facilitating the incubation of **startups and innovators** in the renewable energy sector.
 
• Both organizations aim to support India's target of achieving **net zero emissions** by 2070 through the adoption of innovative renewable energy technologies.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE):**

 
 
• The **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy** is a Government of India ministry that promotes clean and renewable energy sources.
 
• It is involved in the development of **solar energy, wind energy, bio-energy**, and **hydropower**.
 
• The MNRE plays a key role in implementing the **National Solar Mission**, which aims to establish India as a global leader in solar energy.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL):**
 
 
• **BHEL** was established in **1964** and has its headquarters in **New Delhi, India**.
 
• It is one of the largest engineering and manufacturing companies in India, focusing on **power plant equipment**.
 
• BHEL has expertise in various sectors, including **thermal, hydro, and nuclear power**, as well as renewable energy technologies such as **solar and wind power**.
 
 
 
• **Green Hydrogen Technology:**
 
 
• **Green hydrogen** is produced using renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, through a process called **electrolysis**.
 
• It is considered a **clean energy source** as it produces no greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Green hydrogen has applications in industries like **transportation, power generation, and manufacturing**.
 
 
 
• **Solar Energy:**
 
 
• **Solar energy** is harnessed from sunlight using technologies such as **solar panels** and **solar thermal systems**.
 
• It is a key component of India's renewable energy strategy, contributing to the reduction of **fossil fuel dependency**.
 
• India aims to achieve **280 GW of solar capacity by 2030** under its renewable energy goals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the MoU:**

 
 
• The collaboration between **MNRE** and **BHEL** is crucial for accelerating the development of **renewable energy technologies** in India.
 
• It aligns with India's commitment to the **Paris Agreement** on climate change and its goal to achieve **net zero emissions by 2070**.
 
• Such initiatives also promote the **Make in India** program by encouraging local manufacturing and innovation in the renewable energy sector.
 
 
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Goals:**
 
 
• India aims to achieve **500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity** by 2030.
 
• It is one of the global leaders in renewable energy, with significant investments in solar, wind, and green hydrogen.
 
• Programs such as the **National Hydrogen Mission** and **National Solar Mission** play a pivotal role in achieving these targets.
